A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CTMSR and contain 20 readable pages, including the supplementary material. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendix algorithms support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original CTMSR benchmark results, runtime measurements, DTM/SDS ablations and qualitative comparisons in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains the original CTMSR experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The architecture, consistency training, DTM loss and inference procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1's references change from Eq. 1 to Eq. 7, aligning its instructions with the SR forward process already specified in v3 Section 3.2.1.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ImageNet and evaluate on ImageNet-Test, RealSR and RealSet65. The appendices retain the same data coverage and visual test examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–8 and the visual comparisons. This includes the GAN and diffusion baselines, SDS ablation comparator, and OSEDiff/AddSR comparison in the appendix.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics and training budgets are unchanged, including 3,000 ImageNet-Test pairs, 256×256 training patches and the Section 4.1 training schedule. Appendix evaluation settings are also retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix B retain the same comparisons of DTM, SDS and training without DTM. The CLIPIQA noise/artifact case study in Appendix B.2 and Figure 6 is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain identical result entries and values, including CTMSR's ImageNet-Test PSNR of 24.73, MUSIQ of 60.142 and Table 3 runtime of 48 ms. Qualitative outputs and reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–25, the trajectory-matching derivation and appendix schedule definitions are unchanged. Algorithm 1 corrects references to an existing equation without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about distillation-free one-step SR, distribution alignment through DTM, perceptual quality and inference efficiency.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations of DTM's benefits, CLIPIQA's tendency to favor noise or artifacts, and the scalability constraints of Stable Diffusion-based methods. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1, lines 7, 17 and 20, now directs computation of perturbed samples to the SR-specific Eq. 7 instead of Eq. 1. This corrects implementation guidance, although supplementary Algorithm 2 retains the old references. Other technical details and the stated code link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 50 references and related-work discussions are retained. Positioning relative to consistency models, score distillation, ResShift, SinSR and Stable Diffusion-based SR is unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to corrected internal equation references and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. The prose, terminology, section sequence and appendix organization remain substantively unchanged.

P2.justification: Small spacing, typography and line-wrap differences appear, notably near the end of Section 4.3 and in some captions. The eight tables, thirteen figures and three algorithms retain their placement and structure; the embedded visual examples are identical.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1's three references helps readers use the intended residual-plus-noise SR process in Eq. 7 rather than the noise-only Eq. 1. This provides a limited improvement in implementation clarity. The scientific evidence is unchanged, and Algorithm 2's retained incorrect references leave the documentation only partially corrected.
